# Billing batch operations

Nightly billing batch writes AR ledger records from invoice totals.

Rollback is manual and reconciliation reports arrive the next morning.

# Legacy Billing Monolith

This fixture represents legacy invoice batch billing.

01 INVOICE-RECORD.
          05 CUSTOMER-ID PIC X(12).
          05 INVOICE-TOTAL PIC 9(9)V99.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. BILLING.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           PERFORM CALCULATE-INVOICE-TOTAL.
           PERFORM WRITE-AR-LEDGER.
       CALCULATE-INVOICE-TOTAL.
           COMPUTE INVOICE-TOTAL = LINE-AMOUNT + TAX-AMOUNT.
       WRITE-AR-LEDGER.
           DISPLAY "WRITE AR LEDGER".

A short Codex-authored LLM per-file understanding card: purpose, technical role, business relevance or none/unknown, relationships visible from the file, confidence and evidence.
Module/source-family synthesis built from Tier 1 cards and direct source inspection: responsibilities, internal relationships, technical drilldown and uncertainty.
Deep behavior review for important flows, interfaces, contracts, state changes, examples, failure paths and side effects.
Decision-level findings, risks, process improvements, refactoring and target-architecture options.

tier_model.completion_rule: Final readiness requires Tier 1 file-card coverage for every included source-inventory file. Deferred files are not completed analysis; they remain gaps until a Tier 1 card exists.
llm_rules: Codex is the LLM executor for generated workpacks; the CLI must not call a direct LLM API or require API credentials.
The Codex LLM step is not an external service state. Codex is already the active in-session executor, so only artifact/readiness contracts can be incomplete or partial.
Do not summarize files from path names alone.
Open each listed file or use an already-opened exact source excerpt before authoring its Tier 1 card.
Use unknown/none when business relevance cannot be proven.
The Codex-authored Tier 1 step is mandatory for every included file; Codex must write the card and place thin evidence in uncertainty or open questions.
Keep evidence exact with file:line references.
Use Tier 1 to prevent blind spots; use Tier 2-4 to explain interactions and decision implications.
